title: Adding autumn flow change raised March flow forecast error by 5.94% with expanding fits at three Arctic gauges in 1981-2011
abstract: We tested whether October-to-November flow change improves March flow forecasts after November flow and a time trend are known. We used ArcticGRO v20261104 at Ob, Lena and Yenisey gauges, with earlier-year fits and 30 common certified test winters in 1981-2011. Adding the change predictor raised equal-river mean squared log-flow error by 5.94%. Conditional 95% three-year block limits for the increase were 0.83% to 11.99%; five-year limits were 1.09% to 12.12%. Last-25-winter fits and models without time trends gave uncertain contrasts. Thus, this added predictor failed in the main model, but the result does not show a general penalty or a physical cause. Few rivers, revised data, regulation, model choice and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, resampling draws, an arithmetic audit and a figure support reproduction. Source and record-level tables remain external.

display.caption: Adding October-to-November flow change raised mean March forecast error in expanding fits. Negative gain means higher error. Lines show conditional 95% three-year block limits. Shorter fits and models without time trends gave uncertain contrasts.
